messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-20260317-931 \u2014 router.proxy.p95 > 900ms for 2m, auto-page to oncall rotation
pagerduty: Notifying on-call: maria
maria: acked, looking at dashboards now
jake: i'm nearby, pulling router pod logs and recent node events
maria: quick glance: two router pods show p95 tails, cpu spikes coincident with a noisy background compaction on node-a
ben: any 5xx or user errors? need to call customers if so
maria: no 5xx, no error-rate creep. only tail latency, small window ~90s
jake: running tail: ```kubectl -n prod logs router-zz-7f -c proxy --since=5m | grep "latency_ms"``` saw a handful of 2-3x spikes, correlated with kubelet eviction throttles
maria: looks like kubelet pushed a background job causing CPU steal, sched latency. autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough for sudden microburst
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-20260317-931 auto-resolved (metric returned to normal)
pagerduty: Incident PD-20260317-931 marked resolved by auto-resolve rule (3m after firing)
ben: ok good. please note in the ticket that customers were not impacted, but routing tail observed
maria: creating a follow-up: add short suppression during cluster maintenance and detect repeated ephemeral spikes before paging
jake: i'll draft a mini-runbook entry: how to check node-systemd jobs, how to correlate kubectl events with latency traces
ben: add a metric annotation so we can see if the autoscaler lagged vs spike time
tom: taking overnight watch, ack. if it comes back i'll escalate to infra oncall
maria: filed RW-9932 (runbook + suppression + metric annotation). attaching Grafana panel and commands used
jake: RW-9932 created, linked to the incident doc
maria: summary: transient node-level CPU steal caused proxy p95 blip, auto-resolved, no user-visible errors, follow-ups created :white_check_mark:
